title.purpose: Board name. The single emphatic type element; 20px in-SVG, 14px in the header bar.

headline.purpose: Focused element label in the comment modal (15px/600).

body.purpose: Controls, modal prose, comment text, detail and subtitle lines (~13px).

label.purpose: Lane and phase captions in lane-label grey; modal element label (12px/600).

micro.purpose: Sticky id watermark (9px/700, .6 opacity) and the 9.5px detail second line.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: The system's only shadow. Lifts the transient comment <dialog> above the flat bench; paired with a rgba(0,0,0,0.4) backdrop.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Hover-to-focus dimming of edges and stickies, and note-state crossfades. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Sticky — Event
components.description: A board element. Fill is the lane colour (domain grammar); 176x74, 8px corners, id watermark + wrapped label + optional detail.
components.html: E1ItemAdded to cartafter checkout starts
components.css: .ds-sticky { position: relative; width: 176px; height: 74px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 8px; border-radius: 8px; background: #FF9F1C; border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.2); color: #222; font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; transition: filter 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-sticky:hover { filter: brightness(0.97); } .ds-sticky:hover, .ds-sticky:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #1a1a1a; } .ds-sticky-id { position: absolute; top: 7px; left: 8px; font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; opacity: 0.6; } .ds-sticky-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-sticky-detail { font-size: 9.5px; opacity: 0.85; margin-top: 2px; }

components.name: Sticky — Hotspot
components.description: An open question / pain point. Deep-red, white text, and the only SQUARED sticky (2px) — a non-colour type tell.
components.html: H1who owns refunds?

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Everyday control (Reload / Export / Plain). Quiet surface-white on a control border.
components.css: .ds-btn { font: inherit; padding: 5px 11px; border: 1px solid #cfcfda; border-radius: 7px; background: #fff; color: #222; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn:hover { background: #f2f2f7; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1A6FAE; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single committing action — Save comment. The live pen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: inherit; padding: 5px 11px; border: 1px solid #1A6FAE; border-radius: 7px; background: #1A6FAE; color: #fff; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #155d92; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1A6FAE; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Connection state. Idle = lavender-grey; Live = quiet green. A signal, not a CTA.
components.css: .ds-status { font-size: 12px; padding: 3px 9px; border-radius: 999px; background: #eef; color: #557; font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-status--live { background: #e6f7ec; color: #1b7a3d; }

components.name: Comment Field
components.description: Note textarea in the comment modal. Shares its vocabulary with the kind <select>.
components.html: <textarea class="ds-field" placeholder="short note — the next session reads this and adjusts the model"></textarea>
components.css: .ds-field { font: inherit; padding: 8px; border: 1px solid #cfcfda; border-radius: 8px; background: #fff; color: #222; min-height: 90px; resize: vertical; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #1A6FAE; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(26,111,174,0.18); }

components.name: Relationship Chip
components.description: Lists a focused element's connectors — the keyboard-readable way to see edges. The id reads in accent.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; align-items: baseline; background: #eef1f4; border-radius: 6px; padding: 1px 7px; color: #334; font-size: 12px; font-family: -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-chip b { color: #1A6FAE; font-weight: 700; }

narrative.overview: faceto is an instrument, and an instrument lights the specimen and gets out of the way. The specimen is the model — the stickies, the lanes, the edges. Everything else (header, status pill, comment modal, diff overlay) is the bench: the stage, the lamp, and the focusing knob. The bench is machined grey and near-white so the only saturated colour on screen belongs to the domain itself. Hovering an element recedes the rest of the board — connectors to 7%, unrelated stickies to 32% — the way a microscope dims the field. You never decorate; you focus.
keyCharacteristics: Instrument-grey, near-white bench (#fbfbfd / #ffffff); colour is reserved for the model.
A single accent — ink-blue #1A6FAE, the live pen — used only where you are acting.
One sans family at fixed (not fluid) sizes; density without noise.
Hover-to-focus as the primary interaction metaphor; motion conveys state, never spectacle.
Colour is never the only signal: lane position, label, and corner shape carry meaning too.

rules.name: The Bench-Is-Grey Rule
rules.body: No saturated colour in the chrome — ever. Every saturated pixel must belong to the domain grammar (a lane) or the live pen (#1A6FAE). If a control or panel wants colour, the answer is a grey or a tint of the ink.

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: A lane is identified by colour AND vertical position AND label — never colour alone. The hotspot reinforces this with a squared corner. Any new state must carry a redundant non-colour cue so a colour-blind user loses nothing.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: No clamp(), no fluid headings. The board is an instrument read at 1:1; type sizes are pixel-exact and stable across viewports. Responsiveness is structural, never typographic.

rules.name: The Flat-Bench Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The only lift in the system is the modal, and only because it is transient. A resting drop shadow on any other surface is wrong — convey grouping with hairline rules and tonal bands.

dos: Do keep every saturated pixel in the domain grammar or the single accent #1A6FAE; the bench stays grey.
Do give every lane/state a redundant non-colour signal — position, label, corner shape, or badge (the Three-Signal Rule).
Do use fixed px type sizes and a single system sans across HTML and SVG.
Do convey depth with hairline rules (#e0e0e6) and 2% tonal bands; reserve the lone shadow (0 18px 50px #0003) for the modal.
Do keep exactly one primary action (the ink-blue Save) per context; everything else is a quiet secondary control.
Do ship a prefers-reduced-motion alternative for every transition, and a visible :focus-visible ring on every control.
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS dashboard: no card grids, hero-metric tiles, gradient accents, or tracked-uppercase section eyebrows.
Don't add heavy or branded chrome: no logos competing with the board, marketing gradients, decorative illustration, or glassmorphism.
Don't drift toward Miro/FigJam maximalism: no floating toolbars, no panels everywhere, no ambient motion or collaboration overload.
Don't make it toy or childish: no bubbly oversized radii, comic fonts, or candy oversaturation; the sticky palette is a fixed domain grammar, not license to decorate the chrome.
Don't put colour in the chrome or a resting shadow on any surface but the modal.
Don't use clamp()/fluid type or let colour be a lane's only signal.
